title: First mention of Polotsk
description: The Primary Chronicle names Polotsk under this year, making it the oldest recorded town in Belarus.

title: Saint Sophia Cathedral in Polotsk
description: Prince Vseslav builds a stone cathedral to rival those of Kyiv and Novgorod.

title: Battle on the Nemiga
description: The sons of Yaroslav the Wise defeat Vseslav of Polotsk in a battle whose chronicle record is the first mention of Minsk.

title: Cross of Saint Euphrosyne
description: The goldsmith Lazar Bohsha makes a jewelled cross for the abbess Euphrosyne, a national relic that has been lost since 1941.

title: Minsk receives Magdeburg rights
description: Grand Duke Alexander grants Minsk self-government under Magdeburg law.

title: Skaryna prints the Psalter
description: Francysk Skaryna of Polotsk prints the Psalter, the first of his Bible books and the start of printing among the East Slavs.

title: Battle of Lesnaya
description: Peter the Great captures the supply train of the Swedish army marching to join Charles XII, weakening it before Poltava.

title: Crossing of the Berezina
description: Napoleon's retreating army forces a crossing of the Berezina and escapes encirclement at the cost of tens of thousands of men.

title: Synod of Polotsk
description: The Uniate bishops are brought to join the Russian Orthodox Church, ending the Greek Catholic Church to which most Belarusians had belonged.

title: Execution of Kastus Kalinouski
description: The leader of the January Uprising in the Belarusian and Lithuanian lands, who wrote the first newspaper in Belarusian, is hanged.

title: First congress of the Russian Social Democrats
description: Nine delegates meeting in secret found the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party, from which the Bolsheviks later emerge.

title: Belarusian People's Republic declared
description: Under German occupation a national council declares Belarus independent, the first modern Belarusian state.

title: Soviet Belarus proclaimed
description: Bolsheviks proclaim the Socialist Soviet Republic of Byelorussia, the forerunner of the Byelorussian SSR.

title: Peace of Riga
description: Poland and Soviet Russia end their war with a treaty that divides the Belarusian lands between them until 1939.

title: Kurapaty killings
description: The Soviet secret police shoot many thousands of people in a forest outside Minsk, where the graves are made public in 1988.

title: Western Belarus joined to the Byelorussian SSR
description: After the Soviet invasion of Poland an assembly elected under Soviet control asks to join the Soviet Union, and the request is granted.

title: Minsk Ghetto created
description: The German occupiers confine the Jews of Minsk to a ghetto, one of the largest in the occupied Soviet Union, and most are later killed.

title: Khatyn massacre
description: A German auxiliary police battalion burns the village of Khatyn with its people, now the memorial to hundreds of destroyed Belarusian villages.

title: Liberation of Minsk
description: The Red Army retakes Minsk during Operation Bagration, which destroys German Army Group Centre.

title: Declaration of State Sovereignty
description: The Supreme Soviet of the Byelorussian SSR declares the republic sovereign.

title: Independence
description: After the failed coup in Moscow the Supreme Soviet gives the sovereignty declaration constitutional force, making Belarus independent.

title: Belovezha Accords
description: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus declare that the Soviet Union has ceased to exist and found the Commonwealth of Independent States.

title: Lukashenko elected president
description: Alexander Lukashenko wins the first presidential election and goes on to hold the office for decades.

title: Referendum of 1996
description: A disputed referendum greatly widens the president's powers and replaces the elected parliament.

title: Union State treaty
description: Belarus and Russia sign a treaty creating a Union State with common institutions.

title: Protests after the 2010 election
description: Police break up a large demonstration against the presidential election result and arrest most of the opposition candidates.
